verdict.rationale: The Pipecat Cloud OpenAPI document says the private API manages "regions", and the framework is open source and self-hostable with local inference, so users can control where agents run. However, nothing documents region choice as a data-storage or residency control, or which data is kept in which region. Missing for 10: explicit data-residency or region-selection docs for stored data (recordings, transcripts, secrets, session data), a list of available regions, residency or compliance guarantees, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: The private API (/v1...) manages agents, secrets, builds, regions, and organization settings.
the open-source voice-agent framework is real, pip-installable, and self-hostable.
Local inference is already supported via Pipecat, you can use ollama or any custom OpenAI endpoint.
